Fixed. Two parts: (1) DeclaratorParser::parse_base_type's struct/union/enum arms now parse inline/anonymous bodies (parse_record_type/parse_enum_type/parse_field_list/parse_enumerator_list) instead of hard-panicking on a missing tag name, using a new CType::Tagged.body: Option<TagBody> to carry inline fields/enumerators. (2) parse_tag_definition's field-splitting (renamed parse_field_items) now joins multiple PPNodes by brace-depth until a top-level ';', instead of assuming one field per physical line, so nested multi-line struct/union member bodies parse correctly; its outer close-brace search now also tracks brace depth instead of matching the first RBrace-looking line, fixing false-positive early termination when a nested body's own closing line was mistaken for the outer one. Also added FieldItem::Conditional so a field guarded by #if/#ifdef inside a struct body is preserved as Conditional<Vec<FieldItem>> in the polyvariant AST and flattened by RecordDecl::eval in eval.rs, mirroring the existing Initializer::Conditional pattern. Also fixed a second, separate blocker hit immediately after: ConstExpr had no StringLit variant, so any string literal in a general expression (e.g. printf("%d\n", ...)) hit UnexpectedToken -- added ConstExpr::StringLit. add.c (ported into tests/fixtures/add.c with printf declared inline instead of #include <stdio.h>, since the FileCheck harness has no -isystem support) now parses and produces correct, regenerated FileCheck output. Misdiagnosed originally: __has_include_next(<...>) already parses (const_expr.rs parse_has_include) and evaluates (evaluate_expr's Call match arm returns 0) correctly -- verified in isolation with both a synthetic #if using it directly and the actual clang stdbool.h through our -isystem path; neither fails. bool.c's real failure ('unexpected tokens after expression') has a different, deeper root cause: macros #define'd inside ANY conditional block (even statically-true '#if 1') are invisible to expand_macros/divergent_macro_conditions once back outside that block, because record_define stores the macro under conjunction(active, branch_condition) = Condition::And(active, branch) unconditionally (pp.rs conjunction()), while lookup requires exact structural equality against the *current* active condition, which reverts to the pre-conditional value after #endif and can never equal the wrapped And(...) it was stored under. This breaks the universal C header-guard idiom (#ifndef GUARD / #define GUARD ... #endif) for any macro defined inside one, not just __has_include_next-driven ones. Minimal repro (no headers needed): '#if 1
#define FOO 42
#endif
int x = FOO;' -- FOO stays an unresolved identifier. Filed the real bug as a new issue; this one is closed since its literal premise doesn't hold.

Fixed: parse_include_directive (src/pp.rs) only recognized '#include', so '#include_next' lines fell through to the generic '#'-prefix catch-all and errored as 'unsupported preprocessor directive'. Added IncludeDirective::Next, parsed by checking the '#include_next' prefix before '#include' (since the latter is a textual prefix of the former). resolve_include's new Next arm searches self.search.system starting just after the directory that resolved the *current* file (matched by parent-path equality against search.system entries), falling back to searching from the start if the current file's directory isn't itself one of the -isystem dirs. Verified against the real repro (tests/upstream/fixtures/aligned_struct.c via libc-shim's stddef.h -> clang resource-dir stddef.h) and against a new committed regression fixture, tests/fixtures/include-next.c (two tiny header dirs under tests/fixtures/include-next-headers/{outer,inner}), which exercises both a macro defined in the outer header and a declaration only present in the inner one reached via #include_next.

While sweeping more upstream fixtures under the real header chain during this work, also fixed two smaller const_expr.rs gaps and one deeper pp.rs gap discovered along the way (all covered by new regression fixtures):
- parse_has_include's <header> loop didn't accept C keyword tokens (e.g. 'float' lexes as Keyword::Float, not Ident), so __has_include_next(<float.h>) failed to parse -- fixed by accepting Token::Keyword too.
- __has_feature/__has_extension/__has_builtin/__has_attribute/__has_cpp_attribute/__building_module weren't recognized by evaluate_expr's Call arm (only __has_include/__has_include_next were), erroring as 'not a constant expression' -- extended the match to treat them the same way (evaluate to 0). New fixture: tests/fixtures/has-feature-predicates.c.
- Directive matching throughout pp.rs assumed no whitespace between '#' and the directive keyword, so clang's own header style ('#  undef', '#  endif', etc.) either errored as unsupported or silently miscounted conditional nesting ('expected #endif'). Added normalize_directive() and applied it at all 3 sites that inspect a line's directive shape. New fixture: tests/fixtures/directive-whitespace.c.

Swept aligned_struct.c/bool.c/atomic_widths.c/c11.c/atoi_atol_prelude_dynamic.c again after these fixes; remaining failures are real, deeper, already-filed gaps: slate-parser-wf8.1.16 (macros #define'd inside a conditional are invisible outside it -- affects offsetof in stddef.h and bool in stdbool.h), slate-parser-wf8.1.17 (extern "C" { } linkage-spec blocks unsupported), slate-parser-wf8.1.18 (string.h/stdlib.h chain, not yet root-caused). cargo test and cargo clippy --tests both clean (one pre-existing, unrelated clippy warning in pp.rs's #undef/#error branches).

Filed slate-parser-qwy for an unrelated pre-existing same-line struct-body bug found along the way.

Generalized concretize_guard() in src/pp.rs from whole-tree equality to a targeted subtree-replacement (replace_subterm): retroactively replaces the exact Not(Defined(guard)) subtree, wherever nested, with Constant(1) once the guard's own branch is known to have defined it, then re-simplifies. Verified against two-level self-nested guards and a -D-driven macro genuinely nested inside a self-fulfilling guard (both resolve correctly, divergence preserved where it should be). Added tests/fixtures/header-guard.c and tests/fixtures/nested-header-guard.c.

The original repro's remaining failure is a separate, unrelated gap (compiler builtin type macros like __UINTPTR_TYPE__ not seeded) -- filed as slate-parser-g6b.
